topics.name: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
topics.blurb: Presentation, diagnosis, grading, securing the aneurysm, and the neurocritical care of SAH and its complications.

topics.name: Cerebral Aneurysms
topics.blurb: Pathophysiology, location, rupture-risk stratification, and microsurgical or endovascular treatment of intracranial aneurysms.

topics.name: Arteriovenous Malformations
topics.blurb: Angioarchitecture, grading, hemorrhage risk, and multimodal management of brain AVMs.

topics.name: Dural Arteriovenous Fistulas
topics.blurb: Classification by venous drainage, cortical venous reflux risk, and treatment of dural and carotid-cavernous fistulas.

topics.name: Cavernous Malformations
topics.blurb: Natural history, imaging, Zabramski types, and surgical decision-making for cavernous malformations including brainstem lesions.

topics.name: Ischemic Stroke
topics.blurb: Penumbra physiology, thrombolysis, thrombectomy trials, and surgical decompression for acute ischemic stroke.

topics.name: Carotid Occlusive Disease
topics.blurb: Stenosis measurement, revascularization trials, endarterectomy and stenting technique and complications.

topics.name: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage
topics.blurb: Etiology, expansion prediction, blood-pressure targets, and surgical indications for non-traumatic intracerebral hemorrhage.

topics.name: Moyamoya Disease
topics.blurb: Progressive steno-occlusive arteriopathy, Suzuki staging, and direct versus indirect revascularization.

topics.name: Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis
topics.blurb: Pathophysiology, imaging signs, anticoagulation, and endovascular treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis.

topics.name: Spinal Vascular Malformations
topics.blurb: Type I-IV classification, congestive myelopathy, and treatment of spinal dural fistulas and AVMs.

topics.name: Cerebral Revascularization
topics.blurb: Indications, technique, and evidence for low- and high-flow extracranial-intracranial bypass.

concepts.name: SAH clinical presentation
concepts.blurb: Recognize thunderclap headache, meningismus, photophobia, and depressed consciousness as the hallmark presentation of aneurysmal SAH.
acgme: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Grading Medical Management Timing

concepts.name: Thunderclap headache
concepts.blurb: Sudden maximal-intensity headache peaking within seconds; mandates SAH workup even when the neurologic exam is normal.
acgme: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Grading Medical Management Timing

concepts.name: Sentinel headache
concepts.blurb: Warning leak headache days to weeks before major rupture; recognizing it allows treatment before catastrophic hemorrhage.
acgme: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Grading Medical Management Timing

concepts.name: Noncontrast CT diagnosis of SAH
concepts.blurb: Hyperdense subarachnoid blood on noncontrast CT; sensitivity exceeds 95% within 6 hours then declines with time.
acgme: Non-Contrast CT Head Interpretation - Hemorrhage Mass Hydrocephalus

concepts.name: LP and xanthochromia
concepts.blurb: When CT is negative but suspicion persists, xanthochromia on spectrophotometry confirms SAH and distinguishes it from a traumatic tap.
acgme: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Grading Medical Management Timing

concepts.name: CTA versus DSA for aneurysm detection
concepts.blurb: CTA is the rapid first-line screen; catheter DSA remains the gold standard for small aneurysms and treatment planning.
acgme: Diagnostic Cerebral Arteriography - Technique and Interpretation

concepts.name: Hunt-Hess clinical grading
concepts.blurb: Clinical SAH severity grades I-V based on headache, meningismus, and consciousness; predicts surgical risk and outcome.
acgme: SAH Grading Scales - Hunt-Hess WFNS and Fisher or Modified Fisher

concepts.name: WFNS grading scale
concepts.blurb: World Federation grade uses GCS plus motor deficit, giving a more objective SAH severity score than Hunt-Hess.
acgme: SAH Grading Scales - Hunt-Hess WFNS and Fisher or Modified Fisher

concepts.name: Fisher scale
concepts.blurb: Original CT grade of subarachnoid blood thickness predicting vasospasm; superseded clinically by the modified Fisher scale.
acgme: SAH Grading Scales - Hunt-Hess WFNS and Fisher or Modified Fisher

concepts.name: Modified Fisher scale
concepts.blurb: Grades cisternal blood thickness and intraventricular hemorrhage to stratify vasospasm risk more reliably than the original Fisher.
acgme: SAH Grading Scales - Hunt-Hess WFNS and Fisher or Modified Fisher

concepts.name: Aneurysm rebleeding
concepts.blurb: Re-rupture of an unsecured aneurysm, highest in the first 24 hours, carrying very high mortality and driving early treatment.
acgme: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Grading Medical Management Timing

concepts.name: Rebleeding prevention measures
concepts.blurb: Blood-pressure control, short-course antifibrinolytics, and prompt aneurysm securing reduce pre-treatment rebleeding risk.
acgme: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Grading Medical Management Timing

concepts.name: Timing of aneurysm treatment
concepts.blurb: Early aneurysm securing within 24-72 hours prevents rebleeding and permits aggressive vasospasm management.
acgme: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Grading Medical Management Timing

concepts.name: Clipping versus coiling decision
concepts.blurb: Choosing surgical clipping or endovascular coiling weighs aneurysm morphology, location, age, and clinical grade.
acgme: Anterior Circulation Aneurysm - Microsurgical Clipping

concepts.name: ISAT trial
concepts.blurb: Randomized trial showing coiling lowered one-year dependency for suitable ruptured aneurysms, but with higher late retreatment and rebleed.
acgme: Aneurysm Coil Embolization - Basic and Balloon or Stent-Assisted

concepts.name: BRAT trial
concepts.blurb: Barrow trial comparing clipping and coiling by intent-to-treat; coiling favored early but with substantial crossover and higher retreatment.
acgme: Anterior Circulation Aneurysm - Microsurgical Clipping

concepts.name: Cerebral vasospasm
concepts.blurb: Angiographic or sonographic arterial narrowing peaking at days 4-14 after SAH, a key but distinct driver of delayed ischemia.
acgme: Cerebral Vasospasm and Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After SAH

concepts.name: Delayed cerebral ischemia
concepts.blurb: Clinical deterioration or infarction after SAH from spasm, microthrombosis, and spreading depolarization; not synonymous with angiographic vasospasm.
acgme: Cerebral Vasospasm and Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After SAH

concepts.name: Transcranial Doppler monitoring
concepts.blurb: Daily TCD velocities and Lindegaard ratio screen for vasospasm noninvasively, prompting confirmatory imaging when elevated.
acgme: Cerebral Vasospasm and Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After SAH

concepts.name: Nimodipine for SAH
concepts.blurb: Oral calcium-channel blocker improving SAH neurologic outcomes; benefit is neuroprotective, not from reversing angiographic spasm.
acgme: Vasospasm Treatment - Nimodipine HHH Therapy Endovascular Rescue

concepts.name: Induced hypertension for DCI
concepts.blurb: Augmenting blood pressure to maintain perfusion through narrowed vessels in symptomatic DCI, replacing classic triple-H therapy.
acgme: Vasospasm Treatment - Nimodipine HHH Therapy Endovascular Rescue

concepts.name: Endovascular spasm rescue
concepts.blurb: Intra-arterial vasodilators and balloon angioplasty for medically refractory symptomatic vasospasm.
acgme: Vasospasm Treatment - Nimodipine HHH Therapy Endovascular Rescue

concepts.name: SAH-related hydrocephalus
concepts.blurb: Acute obstructive or communicating hydrocephalus from blood blocking CSF flow and arachnoid absorption; managed with EVD then possible shunt.
acgme: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Grading Medical Management Timing

concepts.name: SIADH versus cerebral salt wasting
concepts.blurb: Hyponatremia after SAH distinguished by volume status: euvolemic SIADH needs fluid restriction, hypovolemic CSW needs salt and volume.
acgme: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Grading Medical Management Timing

concepts.name: Neurogenic stunned myocardium
concepts.blurb: Catecholamine surge after SAH causes troponin rise, ECG changes, and Takotsubo-pattern dysfunction mimicking acute coronary syndrome.
acgme: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Grading Medical Management Timing

concepts.name: Neurogenic pulmonary edema
concepts.blurb: Acute sympathetic-surge pulmonary edema after severe SAH, complicating oxygenation and hemodynamic management.
acgme: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Grading Medical Management Timing

concepts.name: Seizure prophylaxis after SAH
concepts.blurb: Brief or selective antiepileptic use after SAH balances seizure risk against drug toxicity; routine prolonged prophylaxis is discouraged.
acgme: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Grading Medical Management Timing

concepts.name: SAH outcome and prognosis
concepts.blurb: Clinical grade, age, rebleeding, and DCI drive SAH outcome, often measured by the modified Rankin Scale.
acgme: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Grading Medical Management Timing

concepts.name: Perimesencephalic SAH
concepts.blurb: Benign non-aneurysmal SAH centered around the midbrain with negative angiography, low rebleed risk, and excellent prognosis.
acgme: Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage - Grading Medical Management Timing

concepts.name: Aneurysm pathophysiology
concepts.blurb: Hemodynamic stress and mural inflammation degrade the internal elastic lamina at branch points, forming and growing aneurysms.
acgme: Neuropathology of Vascular Lesions - Infarction Hemorrhage Aneurysm Wall Histology

concepts.name: Saccular berry aneurysm
concepts.blurb: Most common intracranial aneurysm: a rounded outpouching with neck and dome arising at arterial bifurcations of the circle of Willis.
acgme: Neuropathology of Vascular Lesions - Infarction Hemorrhage Aneurysm Wall Histology

concepts.name: Common aneurysm locations
concepts.blurb: Aneurysms cluster at anterior communicating, posterior communicating, MCA bifurcation, and basilar apex along the circle of Willis.
acgme: Circle of Willis Anatomy and Cerebrovascular Territories

concepts.name: Anterior communicating artery aneurysm
concepts.blurb: Most common ruptured aneurysm; complex perforator anatomy and risk of memory or hypothalamic injury complicate surgery.
acgme: Anterior Circulation Aneurysm - Microsurgical Clipping

concepts.name: Posterior communicating artery aneurysm
concepts.blurb: Arises at the ICA-PCom junction; classically presents with a painful pupil-involving third nerve palsy.
acgme: Anterior Circulation Aneurysm - Microsurgical Clipping

concepts.name: MCA bifurcation aneurysm
concepts.blurb: Wide-necked aneurysm incorporating M2 branches; often favors microsurgical clipping over coiling for branch preservation.
acgme: Anterior Circulation Aneurysm - Microsurgical Clipping

concepts.name: Basilar apex aneurysm
concepts.blurb: Posterior circulation aneurysm with deep, perforator-rich exposure; usually preferentially treated endovascularly.
acgme: Posterior Circulation Aneurysm (Basilar PICA VA) - Endovascular and Surgical

concepts.name: PICA and vertebral aneurysm
concepts.blurb: Vertebral-PICA aneurysms risk lower cranial nerve and brainstem injury; treatment balances clipping, coiling, and vessel sacrifice.
acgme: Posterior Circulation Aneurysm (Basilar PICA VA) - Endovascular and Surgical

concepts.name: Third nerve palsy from PCom aneurysm
concepts.blurb: Pupil-involving oculomotor palsy from compression signals an enlarging PCom aneurysm and warrants urgent evaluation.
acgme: Cranial Nerves I-XII - Anatomy Nuclei and Clinical Syndromes

concepts.name: Unruptured aneurysm management
concepts.blurb: Treat or observe unruptured aneurysms by weighing rupture risk against treatment risk, age, and patient preference.
acgme: Anterior Circulation Aneurysm - Microsurgical Clipping

concepts.name: ISUIA study
concepts.blurb: Landmark study reporting low rupture rates for small anterior unruptured aneurysms, shaping conservative management debate.
acgme: Anterior Circulation Aneurysm - Microsurgical Clipping

concepts.name: PHASES rupture-risk score
concepts.blurb: Aggregates population, hypertension, age, size, prior SAH, and location to estimate five-year unruptured aneurysm rupture risk.
acgme: Anterior Circulation Aneurysm - Microsurgical Clipping

concepts.name: UCAS Japan study
concepts.blurb: Prospective cohort quantifying unruptured aneurysm rupture risk by size and location, informing the PHASES model.
acgme: Anterior Circulation Aneurysm - Microsurgical Clipping

concepts.name: Giant aneurysm
concepts.blurb: Aneurysm 25 mm or larger, often partially thrombosed, presenting with mass effect and frequently requiring bypass or flow diversion.
acgme: Flow-Diverting Stent (Pipeline Embolization Device) - Indications and Technique

concepts.name: Blister aneurysm
concepts.blurb: Fragile broad-based dorsal ICA wall defect lacking a true neck; high rupture risk and treatment failure.
acgme: Flow-Diverting Stent (Pipeline Embolization Device) - Indications and Technique

concepts.name: Mycotic aneurysm
concepts.blurb: Infectious distal aneurysm from septic emboli, typically endocarditis; often managed medically with antibiotics and serial imaging.
acgme: Neuropathology of Vascular Lesions - Infarction Hemorrhage Aneurysm Wall Histology

concepts.name: Dissecting aneurysm
concepts.blurb: Intramural blood from an intimal tear creating a pseudoaneurysm, often vertebral, presenting with ischemia or SAH.
acgme: Posterior Circulation Aneurysm (Basilar PICA VA) - Endovascular and Surgical

concepts.name: Fusiform aneurysm
concepts.blurb: Circumferential dilation lacking a defined neck, often atherosclerotic or dolichoectatic, complicating reconstructive treatment.
acgme: Neuropathology of Vascular Lesions - Infarction Hemorrhage Aneurysm Wall Histology

concepts.name: Microsurgical aneurysm clipping
concepts.blurb: Open exclusion of the aneurysm with a clip across the neck while preserving parent and perforating vessels.
acgme: Anterior Circulation Aneurysm - Microsurgical Clipping

concepts.name: Endovascular coil embolization
concepts.blurb: Transarterial packing of the aneurysm dome with detachable coils to induce thrombosis and exclude it from circulation.
acgme: Aneurysm Coil Embolization - Basic and Balloon or Stent-Assisted

concepts.name: Balloon and stent-assisted coiling
concepts.blurb: Adjuncts for wide-necked aneurysms; stents require dual antiplatelet therapy, limiting use in the acute ruptured setting.
acgme: Aneurysm Coil Embolization - Basic and Balloon or Stent-Assisted

concepts.name: Flow-diverting stent
concepts.blurb: Dense-mesh stent redirecting flow to thrombose the aneurysm and remodel the parent vessel, mainly for large or wide-necked ICA aneurysms.
acgme: Flow-Diverting Stent (Pipeline Embolization Device) - Indications and Technique

concepts.name: Intraoperative aneurysm rupture
concepts.blurb: Premature rupture during dissection or clipping managed with suction, proximal control, and temporary clipping to regain the field.
acgme: Anterior Circulation Aneurysm - Microsurgical Clipping

concepts.name: Temporary clipping and adenosine
concepts.blurb: Brief proximal occlusion or adenosine-induced flow arrest softens the aneurysm for safe dissection and clip placement.
acgme: Anterior Circulation Aneurysm - Microsurgical Clipping

concepts.name: AVM clinical presentation
concepts.blurb: Brain AVMs present with hemorrhage, seizures, focal deficit, or headache, most often in young adults.
acgme: Cerebral AVM - Spetzler-Martin Grading and Treatment Decision-Making

concepts.name: AVM angioarchitecture
concepts.blurb: An AVM is a nidus of arteriovenous shunting without intervening capillaries, fed by arteries and drained by arterialized veins.
acgme: Cerebral AVM - Spetzler-Martin Grading and Treatment Decision-Making

concepts.name: AVM feeders, nidus, and drainage
concepts.blurb: Defining feeding arteries, nidus compactness, and deep versus superficial venous drainage guides grading and treatment.
acgme: Cerebral AVM - Spetzler-Martin Grading and Treatment Decision-Making

concepts.name: AVM hemorrhage risk
concepts.blurb: Annual rupture risk near 2-4% rises with prior hemorrhage, deep location, deep venous drainage, and associated aneurysms.
acgme: Cerebral AVM - Spetzler-Martin Grading and Treatment Decision-Making

concepts.name: Spetzler-Martin grading
concepts.blurb: Sums points for AVM size, eloquence, and deep venous drainage to predict microsurgical risk on a I-V scale.
acgme: Cerebral AVM - Spetzler-Martin Grading and Treatment Decision-Making

concepts.name: Supplementary Lawton-Young grade
concepts.blurb: Adds age, hemorrhagic presentation, and nidus diffuseness to Spetzler-Martin for refined surgical risk prediction.
acgme: AVM Microsurgical Resection - Grade I-II and Infratentorial

concepts.name: ARUBA trial
concepts.blurb: Trial finding medical management superior to intervention for unruptured AVMs at short follow-up; criticized for selection and follow-up limits.
acgme: Cerebral AVM - Spetzler-Martin Grading and Treatment Decision-Making

concepts.name: AVM embolization
concepts.blurb: Endovascular nidus or feeder occlusion, usually adjunctive before resection or radiosurgery and rarely curative alone.
acgme: Cerebral AVM - Spetzler-Martin Grading and Treatment Decision-Making

concepts.name: AVM radiosurgery
concepts.blurb: Stereotactic radiation obliterating small or deep AVMs over 2-3 years, with latency hemorrhage risk until obliteration.
acgme: AVM Radiosurgery - Staged Treatment for Larger Lesions

concepts.name: AVM microsurgical resection
concepts.blurb: Circumferential dissection ligating feeders before the draining vein, achieving immediate cure for low-grade AVMs.
acgme: AVM Microsurgical Resection - Grade I-II and Infratentorial

concepts.name: AVM-associated aneurysms
concepts.blurb: Flow-related feeder or intranidal aneurysms increase hemorrhage risk and often dictate treatment priority.
acgme: Cerebral AVM - Spetzler-Martin Grading and Treatment Decision-Making

concepts.name: Normal perfusion pressure breakthrough
concepts.blurb: Postresection hyperemia and hemorrhage in chronically hypoperfused brain after large AVM removal; mitigated by staged treatment.
acgme: AVM Microsurgical Resection - Grade I-II and Infratentorial

concepts.name: Dural AVF pathophysiology
concepts.blurb: Acquired arteriovenous shunt within the dura, often near a sinus, frequently linked to prior thrombosis or venous hypertension.
acgme: Dural Arteriovenous Fistula - Classification (Cognard or Borden) and Treatment

concepts.name: Dural AVF presentation
concepts.blurb: Presents with pulsatile tinnitus, ophthalmic symptoms, or, with venous reflux, hemorrhage and neurologic deficit.
acgme: Dural Arteriovenous Fistula - Classification (Cognard or Borden) and Treatment

concepts.name: Borden classification
concepts.blurb: Three-tier dural AVF scheme by venous drainage; cortical venous drainage (types II-III) marks aggressive lesions.
acgme: Dural Arteriovenous Fistula - Classification (Cognard or Borden) and Treatment

concepts.name: Cognard classification
concepts.blurb: Five-type dural AVF scheme grading sinus flow direction and cortical venous reflux to stratify hemorrhage risk.
acgme: Dural Arteriovenous Fistula - Classification (Cognard or Borden) and Treatment

concepts.name: Cortical venous reflux
concepts.blurb: Retrograde flow into cortical veins is the key feature raising dural AVF hemorrhage and neurologic risk, mandating treatment.
acgme: Dural Arteriovenous Fistula - Classification (Cognard or Borden) and Treatment

concepts.name: Carotid-cavernous fistula
concepts.blurb: Shunt into the cavernous sinus; direct high-flow (often traumatic) versus indirect dural types differ in presentation and treatment.
acgme: Dural Arteriovenous Fistula - Classification (Cognard or Borden) and Treatment

concepts.name: Dural AVF treatment
concepts.blurb: Transvenous or transarterial embolization, sometimes surgical disconnection, targeting the fistulous point and abolishing cortical reflux.
acgme: Dural Arteriovenous Fistula - Classification (Cognard or Borden) and Treatment

concepts.name: Cavernous malformation pathology
concepts.blurb: Angiographically occult cluster of thin-walled sinusoidal caverns without intervening brain, prone to recurrent small hemorrhages.
acgme: Cavernous Malformation - Natural History and Surgical Indications

concepts.name: Cavernoma natural history
concepts.blurb: Low annual bleed risk for supratentorial lesions, higher after prior hemorrhage and for brainstem location, guiding observation.
acgme: Cavernous Malformation - Natural History and Surgical Indications

concepts.name: Cavernoma imaging
concepts.blurb: Popcorn lesion with mixed-signal core and hemosiderin rim, best seen on gradient-echo or susceptibility-weighted MRI.
acgme: Brain MRI Sequences - T1 T2 FLAIR DWI SWI T1Gad - Clinical Application

concepts.name: Zabramski classification
concepts.blurb: MRI types I-IV of cavernous malformation by hemorrhage age and signal, aiding lesion characterization and follow-up.
acgme: Cavernous Malformation - Natural History and Surgical Indications

concepts.name: Developmental venous anomaly association
concepts.blurb: Cavernomas often coexist with a developmental venous anomaly that must be preserved at surgery to avoid venous infarction.
acgme: Cavernous Malformation - Natural History and Surgical Indications

concepts.name: Brainstem cavernoma surgery
concepts.blurb: Resection considered after repeat symptomatic hemorrhage when the lesion reaches a pial or ependymal surface via a safe entry zone.
acgme: Brainstem Cavernoma - Surgical Approach and Timing

concepts.name: Familial cavernous malformations
concepts.blurb: Autosomal dominant CCM gene mutations cause multiple lesions and higher de novo formation and hemorrhage rates.
acgme: Cavernous Malformation - Natural History and Surgical Indications

concepts.name: Ischemic penumbra
concepts.blurb: Hypoperfused but salvageable tissue around the infarct core; preserving it is the rationale for reperfusion therapy.
acgme: Ischemic Stroke - IV tPA Eligibility Timing Windows and Treatment Algorithm

concepts.name: Stroke vascular syndromes
concepts.blurb: Recognizing MCA, ACA, and posterior circulation syndromes localizes the occlusion and guides imaging triage.
acgme: Circle of Willis Anatomy and Cerebrovascular Territories

concepts.name: NIH Stroke Scale
concepts.blurb: Standardized 0-42 deficit score quantifying stroke severity, guiding treatment decisions, and predicting outcome.
acgme: Ischemic Stroke - IV tPA Eligibility Timing Windows and Treatment Algorithm

concepts.name: IV thrombolysis with alteplase
concepts.blurb: Intravenous alteplase restores flow when given within the time window, with hemorrhage risk requiring strict eligibility screening.
acgme: Ischemic Stroke - IV tPA Eligibility Timing Windows and Treatment Algorithm

concepts.name: tPA windows and contraindications
concepts.blurb: Alteplase within 3-4.5 hours of onset; recent hemorrhage, surgery, coagulopathy, and uncontrolled hypertension are key exclusions.
acgme: Ischemic Stroke - IV tPA Eligibility Timing Windows and Treatment Algorithm

concepts.name: Tenecteplase for stroke
concepts.blurb: Single-bolus fibrinolytic with comparable or better reperfusion than alteplase, increasingly favored before thrombectomy.
acgme: Ischemic Stroke - IV tPA Eligibility Timing Windows and Treatment Algorithm

concepts.name: Endovascular thrombectomy indications
concepts.blurb: Mechanical thrombectomy for large-vessel occlusion, standard within 6 hours and extendable with favorable imaging selection.
acgme: Acute Ischemic Stroke - Endovascular Thrombectomy (ICA M1 BA)

concepts.name: DAWN trial
concepts.blurb: Showed thrombectomy benefit up to 24 hours using clinical-core mismatch selection in late-window large-vessel occlusion.
acgme: Acute Ischemic Stroke - Endovascular Thrombectomy (ICA M1 BA)

concepts.name: DEFUSE 3 trial
concepts.blurb: Extended thrombectomy to 16 hours using perfusion core-penumbra mismatch, complementing DAWN selection criteria.
acgme: Acute Ischemic Stroke - Endovascular Thrombectomy (ICA M1 BA)

concepts.name: Large-core thrombectomy trials
concepts.blurb: SELECT2 and ANGEL-ASPECT extended thrombectomy benefit to large established infarcts, broadening treatable patients.
acgme: Acute Ischemic Stroke - Endovascular Thrombectomy (ICA M1 BA)

concepts.name: CT perfusion mismatch
concepts.blurb: Perfusion imaging separates infarct core from salvageable penumbra to select late-window reperfusion candidates.
acgme: CT Angiography and CT Perfusion - Stroke and Vascular Pathology Interpretation

concepts.name: ASPECTS score
concepts.blurb: Ten-point CT topographic score of early MCA ischemic change; lower scores indicate larger core and worse prognosis.
acgme: Non-Contrast CT Head Interpretation - Hemorrhage Mass Hydrocephalus

concepts.name: Malignant MCA infarction
concepts.blurb: Large MCA infarct with progressive edema and herniation, signaled by declining consciousness and midline shift.
acgme: Acute Ischemic Stroke - Endovascular Thrombectomy (ICA M1 BA)

concepts.name: Decompressive hemicraniectomy
concepts.blurb: Large bone-flap removal and duraplasty relieving pressure in malignant MCA infarction to reduce mortality.
acgme: Acute Ischemic Stroke - Endovascular Thrombectomy (ICA M1 BA)

concepts.name: Hemicraniectomy stroke trials
concepts.blurb: Pooled DECIMAL, DESTINY, and HAMLET data show early hemicraniectomy reduces mortality with more survivors at moderate disability.
acgme: Acute Ischemic Stroke - Endovascular Thrombectomy (ICA M1 BA)

concepts.name: Cerebellar infarction surgery
concepts.blurb: Suboccipital decompression for swelling cerebellar infarct causing brainstem compression or fourth-ventricle obstruction.
acgme: Distal Vessel Thrombectomy (M2 P1 Cerebellar) - Complex Endovascular

concepts.name: Cervical artery dissection
concepts.blurb: Carotid or vertebral intimal tear causing stroke in younger patients; usually managed with antithrombotic therapy.
acgme: Vertebrobasilar Insufficiency - Diagnosis and Endovascular Treatment

concepts.name: Hemorrhagic transformation
concepts.blurb: Bleeding into infarcted tissue, increased by reperfusion therapy and large infarcts, ranging from petechiae to parenchymal hematoma.
acgme: Ischemic Stroke - IV tPA Eligibility Timing Windows and Treatment Algorithm

concepts.name: Carotid atherosclerosis pathophysiology
concepts.blurb: Plaque at the carotid bifurcation causes stroke through artery-to-artery embolism or flow-limiting stenosis.
acgme: Carotid Endarterectomy - Indications and Surgical Technique

concepts.name: Carotid stenosis measurement
concepts.blurb: NASCET-method percent stenosis from angiography, duplex, or CTA defines severity and treatment thresholds.
acgme: Carotid Endarterectomy - Indications and Surgical Technique

concepts.name: Symptomatic versus asymptomatic stenosis
concepts.blurb: Symptomatic stenosis carries higher stroke risk and lower treatment thresholds than asymptomatic disease.
acgme: Carotid Endarterectomy - Indications and Surgical Technique

concepts.name: NASCET trial
concepts.blurb: Established endarterectomy benefit for symptomatic high-grade carotid stenosis, defining the standard measurement method.
acgme: Carotid Endarterectomy - Indications and Surgical Technique

concepts.name: ACAS trial
concepts.blurb: Showed modest endarterectomy benefit for asymptomatic high-grade stenosis, contingent on low surgical complication rates.
acgme: Carotid Endarterectomy - Indications and Surgical Technique

concepts.name: CREST trial
concepts.blurb: Compared stenting and endarterectomy; similar composite outcome, with more periprocedural stroke after stenting and more MI after surgery.
acgme: Carotid Artery Stenting - Indications and Comparison to CEA

concepts.name: Carotid endarterectomy technique
concepts.blurb: Arteriotomy with plaque removal, selective shunting, and patch or primary closure under monitoring of cerebral perfusion.
acgme: Carotid Endarterectomy - Indications and Surgical Technique

concepts.name: Carotid endarterectomy complications
concepts.blurb: Perioperative stroke, cranial nerve injury, neck hematoma, restenosis, and hyperperfusion threaten endarterectomy outcomes.
acgme: Carotid Endarterectomy - Indications and Surgical Technique

concepts.name: Carotid artery stenting
concepts.blurb: Endovascular stenting with embolic protection, favored for surgically high-risk necks but with higher periprocedural stroke in elders.
acgme: Carotid Artery Stenting - Indications and Comparison to CEA

concepts.name: Cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome
concepts.blurb: Headache, seizures, or hemorrhage from restored flow into a chronically hypoperfused, autoregulation-impaired hemisphere after revascularization.
acgme: Carotid Endarterectomy - Indications and Surgical Technique

concepts.name: Carotid web
concepts.blurb: Shelf-like intimal fibromuscular dysplasia at the carotid bulb causing recurrent embolic stroke in younger patients.
acgme: Carotid Endarterectomy - Indications and Surgical Technique

concepts.name: Intracerebral hemorrhage etiology
concepts.blurb: Spontaneous ICH arises from hypertension, amyloid angiopathy, vascular malformations, coagulopathy, tumors, or drugs.
acgme: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage - Medical and Surgical Management

concepts.name: Hypertensive hemorrhage locations
concepts.blurb: Hypertensive ICH favors basal ganglia, thalamus, pons, and cerebellum from small perforator vessel rupture.
acgme: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage - Medical and Surgical Management

concepts.name: ICH clinical presentation
concepts.blurb: Sudden focal deficit with headache, vomiting, and declining consciousness reflecting hematoma location and mass effect.
acgme: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage - Medical and Surgical Management

concepts.name: ICH score
concepts.blurb: Mortality prediction from GCS, volume, infratentorial origin, intraventricular extension, and age.
acgme: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage - Medical and Surgical Management

concepts.name: CTA spot sign
concepts.blurb: Contrast extravasation within the hematoma on CTA predicting ongoing bleeding and hematoma expansion.
acgme: CT Angiography and CT Perfusion - Stroke and Vascular Pathology Interpretation

concepts.name: Hematoma expansion
concepts.blurb: Early hematoma growth worsening outcome, motivating blood-pressure control and reversal of coagulopathy.
acgme: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage - Medical and Surgical Management

concepts.name: ICH blood pressure management
concepts.blurb: Early systolic lowering toward 140 mmHg is safe and may limit expansion, without clear functional outcome benefit.
acgme: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage - Medical and Surgical Management

concepts.name: ATACH-2 and INTERACT2 trials
concepts.blurb: Trials defining intensive blood-pressure lowering in acute ICH: safe but without significant disability reduction.
acgme: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage - Medical and Surgical Management

concepts.name: STICH and STICH II trials
concepts.blurb: Showed no overall benefit of early surgery for supratentorial ICH; possible benefit for superficial lobar clots without IVH.
acgme: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage - Medical and Surgical Management

concepts.name: MISTIE III trial
concepts.blurb: Minimally invasive catheter aspiration with thrombolysis was safe but did not improve outcome unless clot was well reduced.
acgme: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage - Medical and Surgical Management

concepts.name: Cerebellar hemorrhage surgery
concepts.blurb: Evacuate cerebellar hematomas over 3 cm or with brainstem compression or hydrocephalus before catastrophic deterioration.
acgme: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage - Medical and Surgical Management

concepts.name: Anticoagulation-associated ICH
concepts.blurb: Reverse warfarin with PCC and vitamin K and direct oral anticoagulants with specific agents to halt expansion.
acgme: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage - Medical and Surgical Management

concepts.name: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy
concepts.blurb: Amyloid deposition in cortical vessels causing recurrent lobar hemorrhage and microbleeds in the elderly.
acgme: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage - Medical and Surgical Management

concepts.name: Moyamoya pathophysiology
concepts.blurb: Progressive stenosis of the supraclinoid ICA with fragile collateral basal vessels predisposing to ischemia and hemorrhage.
acgme: Moyamoya Disease - Diagnosis Angiographic Staging and Revascularization

concepts.name: Moyamoya presentation
concepts.blurb: Children present with ischemia, often triggered by hyperventilation; adults more often present with hemorrhage.
acgme: Moyamoya Disease - Diagnosis Angiographic Staging and Revascularization

concepts.name: Suzuki angiographic staging
concepts.blurb: Six angiographic stages tracking ICA narrowing, the puff-of-smoke collaterals, and transdural recruitment in moyamoya.
acgme: Moyamoya Disease - Diagnosis Angiographic Staging and Revascularization

concepts.name: Moyamoya imaging
concepts.blurb: MRI ivy sign, basal collaterals, and perfusion studies assess ischemic burden and revascularization need.
acgme: Moyamoya Disease - Diagnosis Angiographic Staging and Revascularization

concepts.name: Direct revascularization for moyamoya
concepts.blurb: STA-MCA anastomosis gives immediate flow augmentation, favored in adults with established hemodynamic compromise.
acgme: STA-MCA Bypass - Indications (Moyamoya Complex Aneurysm) and Technique

concepts.name: Indirect revascularization for moyamoya
concepts.blurb: Procedures like EDAS lay vascularized tissue on the cortex to grow collaterals, preferred in children.
acgme: Moyamoya Disease - Diagnosis Angiographic Staging and Revascularization

concepts.name: CVST pathophysiology
concepts.blurb: Dural sinus or cortical vein thrombosis raises venous pressure, causing edema, venous infarction, and hemorrhage.
acgme: Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis - Diagnosis and Management

concepts.name: CVST presentation
concepts.blurb: Headache, raised intracranial pressure, seizures, or non-arterial-territory infarcts should prompt venous imaging.
acgme: Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis - Diagnosis and Management

concepts.name: CVST imaging
concepts.blurb: CT or MR venography shows the filling defect; the empty delta sign indicates superior sagittal sinus thrombosis.
acgme: Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis - Diagnosis and Management

concepts.name: CVST etiology
concepts.blurb: Prothrombotic states, pregnancy, oral contraceptives, dehydration, infection, and malignancy predispose to venous thrombosis.
acgme: Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis - Diagnosis and Management

concepts.name: CVST anticoagulation
concepts.blurb: Anticoagulation is first-line even with venous hemorrhage, halting thrombus propagation and improving outcome.
acgme: Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis - Diagnosis and Management

concepts.name: CVST endovascular and surgical rescue
concepts.blurb: Endovascular thrombectomy or decompressive surgery is reserved for deterioration despite anticoagulation.
acgme: Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis - Diagnosis and Management

concepts.name: Spinal vascular malformation classification
concepts.blurb: Type I-IV scheme separates dural fistula, glomus, juvenile, and perimedullary lesions, guiding treatment strategy.
acgme: Dural Arteriovenous Fistula - Classification (Cognard or Borden) and Treatment

concepts.name: Spinal dural AVF (type I)
concepts.blurb: Most common spinal vascular malformation; low-flow dural shunt causing venous congestion and progressive myelopathy in older men.
acgme: Dural Arteriovenous Fistula - Classification (Cognard or Borden) and Treatment

concepts.name: Foix-Alajouanine syndrome
concepts.blurb: Progressive necrotizing myelopathy from chronic venous hypertension in an untreated spinal dural fistula.
acgme: Dural Arteriovenous Fistula - Classification (Cognard or Borden) and Treatment

concepts.name: Intramedullary glomus and juvenile AVM
concepts.blurb: High-flow intramedullary (type II) and extensive juvenile (type III) AVMs present with hemorrhage in younger patients.
acgme: Dural Arteriovenous Fistula - Classification (Cognard or Borden) and Treatment

concepts.name: Spinal vascular malformation presentation
concepts.blurb: Progressive myelopathy and gait decline from venous congestion, or acute deficit from hemorrhage in high-flow lesions.
acgme: Dural Arteriovenous Fistula - Classification (Cognard or Borden) and Treatment

concepts.name: Spinal vascular malformation treatment
concepts.blurb: Disconnect the fistula or embolize the nidus; identifying the artery of Adamkiewicz is essential to avoid cord infarction.
acgme: Dural Arteriovenous Fistula - Classification (Cognard or Borden) and Treatment

concepts.name: Cerebral bypass indications
concepts.blurb: Bypass is used for flow augmentation in moyamoya or hemodynamic ischemia and for flow replacement when a vessel is sacrificed.
acgme: STA-MCA Bypass - Indications (Moyamoya Complex Aneurysm) and Technique

concepts.name: STA-MCA bypass
concepts.blurb: Low-flow superficial temporal to middle cerebral artery anastomosis for flow augmentation, the workhorse direct bypass.
acgme: STA-MCA Bypass - Indications (Moyamoya Complex Aneurysm) and Technique

concepts.name: High-flow bypass
concepts.blurb: Interposition vein or radial-artery graft replacing major vessel flow when sacrificing a carotid for giant or complex aneurysms.
acgme: STA-MCA Bypass - Indications (Moyamoya Complex Aneurysm) and Technique

concepts.name: EC-IC bypass trials
concepts.blurb: The EC-IC Bypass Study and COSS showed no benefit over medical therapy for atherosclerotic carotid occlusion despite improved perfusion.
acgme: STA-MCA Bypass - Indications (Moyamoya Complex Aneurysm) and Technique

concepts.name: Bypass patency assessment
concepts.blurb: Intraoperative indocyanine-green angiography, micro-Doppler, and flowmetry confirm anastomosis patency before closure.
acgme: STA-MCA Bypass - Indications (Moyamoya Complex Aneurysm) and Technique

concepts.name: Vein of Galen malformation
concepts.blurb: Neonatal high-flow arteriovenous shunt into the median prosencephalic vein causing heart failure; managed by staged embolization (see pediatric).
acgme: Dural Arteriovenous Fistula - Classification (Cognard or Borden) and Treatment
